[list-style:none] min-w-0 shrink"><a class="vp-raw transition-colors hover:text-(--Labels-Primary) whitespace-nowrap" href="/en/blog/"><span class="block overflow-hidden min-w-0 whitespace-nowrap shrink text-ellipsis">Research</span></a></li></ol></nav></div><section class="pb-20 w-full"><div class="max-w-none markdown"><h1 node="[object Object]">Kimi K2.5: Visual Agentic Intelligence</h1>
<p>Today, we are introducing Kimi K2.5, the most powerful open-source model to date.</p>
<p>Kimi K2.5 builds on Kimi K2 with continued pretraining over approximately 15T mixed visual and text tokens. Built as a native multimodal model, K2.5 delivers state-of-the-art <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">coding and vision</strong> capabilities and a self-directed <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">agent swarm</strong> paradigm.</p>
<p>For complex tasks, Kimi K2.5 can self-direct an <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">agent swarm</strong> with up to 100 sub-agents, executing parallel workflows across up to <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">1,500</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">tool calls</strong>. Compared with a single-agent setup, this reduces execution time by up to <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">4.5x</strong>. The agent swarm is automatically created and orchestrated by Kimi K2.5 without any predefined subagents or workflow.</p>
<p>Kimi K2.5 is available via <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="/en" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">Kimi.com</a>, the Kimi App, the <a href="https://platform.kimi.com/" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">API</a>, and <a href="/code/en" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">Kimi Code</a></strong>. Kimi.com &amp; Kimi App now supports 4 modes: K2.5 Instant, K2.5 Thinking, K2.5 Agent, and K2.5 Agent Swarm (Beta). Agent Swarm is currently in beta on Kimi.com, with free credits available for high-tier paid users.</p>
<!--$?--><template id="B:0"></template><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<div style="margin:24px auto;max-width:480px;padding-top:16px">
  <img src="https://statics.kimi.ai/blogs/k2-5/token_cost.png" alt="" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/>
</div>
<blockquote class="border-l-4 border-(--Colors-KMBlue) bg-(--Fills-F1) px-5 py-4 rounded-r-lg rounded-l-none my-6 [&amp;_p]:m-0 [&amp;_p]:text-(--Labels-Primary)">
<p>Across three agentic benchmarks—HLE, BrowseComp, and SWE-Verified—Kimi K2.5 delivers strong performance at a fraction of the cost.</p>
</blockquote>
<h2 node="[object Object]">1. Coding with Vision</h2>
<p>Kimi K2.5 is the strongest open-source model to date for coding, with particularly strong capabilities in front-end development.</p>
<p>K2.5 can turn simple conversations into complete front-end interfaces, implementing <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">interactive layouts</strong> and <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">rich animations such as scroll-triggered effects</strong>. Below are examples generated by K2.5 from a single prompt with image-gen tool:</p>
<div data-blog-hero-width="true"><div class="my-4 animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)" style="min-height:320px"></div></div>
<p>Beyond text prompts, K2.5 excels at <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">coding with vision</strong>. By reasoning over images and video, K2.5 improves image/video-to-code generation and visual debugging, lowering the barrier for users to express intent visually.</p>
<p>Here is an example of K2.5 reconstructing a website from video:</p>
<div data-blog-hero-width="true"><div class="my-4 animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)" style="min-height:320px"></div></div>
<p>This capability stems from massive-scale vision-text joint pre-training. At scale, the trade-off between vision and text capabilities disappears — they improve in unison.</p>
<p>Below is an example of K2.5 reasoning over a puzzle and marking the shortest path using code:</p>
<!--$?--><template id="B:1"></template><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">K2.5 excels in real-world software engineering tasks.</strong> We evaluate it using <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Kimi Code Bench</strong>, our <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">internal coding benchmark</strong> covering diverse end-to-end tasks — from building to debugging, refactoring, testing, and scripting — across multiple programming languages. On this benchmark, <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">K2.5 shows consistent and meaningful improvements over</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">K2</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">across task types</strong>.</p>
<div style="margin:24px auto;max-width:480px;padding-top:16px">
  <img src="https://statics.kimi.ai/blogs/k2-5/img_v3_02ub_47858019-34ce-4e34-ae76-f7165f95b91g.png" alt="" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/>
</div>
<p>To try out K2.5&#x27;s agentic coding capabilities, <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="/en/agent" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">K2.5 Agent</a></strong> offers a set of preconfigured tools for immediate, hands-on experiences. For software engineering use cases, we recommend pairing Kimi K2.5 with our new coding product, <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="/code/en" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">Kimi Code</a></strong>.</p>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="/code/en" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">Kimi Code</a></strong> works in your terminal and can be integrated with various IDEs including VSCode, Cursor, Zed, etc. Kimi Code is open-sourced and supports images and videos as inputs. It also automatically discovers and migrates existing skills and MCPs into your working environment in Kimi Code.</p>
<p>Here&#x27;s an example using <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="/code/en" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">Kimi Code</a></strong> to translate the aesthetic of <em class="italic text-(--Labels-Secondary)">Matisse&#x27;s La Danse</em> into the Kimi App. This demo highlights a breakthrough in <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">autonomous visual debugging</strong>. Using visual inputs and documentation lookup, K2.5 visually inspects its own output and iterates on it autonomously. It creates an art-inspired webpage created end to end:</p>
<div data-blog-hero-width="true"><div class="my-4 animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)" style="min-height:320px"></div></div>
<h2 node="[object Object]">2. Agent Swarm</h2>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Scaling Out, Not Just Up.</strong> We release <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="/en/agent-swarm" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">K2.5 Agent Swarm</a></strong> as a research preview, marking a shift from single-agent scaling to self-directed, coordinated swarm-like execution.</p>
<p>Trained with Parallel-Agent Reinforcement Learning (PARL), K2.5 learns to self-direct an <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">agent swarm</strong> of up to <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">100 sub-agents</strong>, executing parallel workflows across <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">up to 1,500 coordinated steps,</strong> without predefined roles or hand-crafted workflows.</p>
<p>PARL uses a <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><em class="italic text-(--Labels-Secondary)">trainable orchestrator agent</em></strong> to decompose tasks into parallelizable subtasks, each executed by dynamically instantiated, <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><em class="italic text-(--Labels-Secondary)">frozen subagents</em></strong>. Running these subtasks concurrently significantly reduces end-to-end latency compared to sequential agent execution.</p>
<p>Training a reliable parallel orchestrator is challenging due to delayed, sparse, and non-stationary feedback from independently running subagents. A common failure mode is <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">serial collapse</strong>, where the orchestrator defaults to single-agent execution despite having parallel capacity. To address this, PARL employs <em class="italic text-(--Labels-Secondary)">staged reward shaping</em> that encourages parallelism early in training and gradually shifts focus toward task success.</p>
<p>We define the reward as</p>

<p>The performance reward <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>perf</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{perf}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7167em;vertical-align:-0.2861em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em">r</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0278em;margin-right:0.05em"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">perf</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2861em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> evaluates the overall success and quality of the solution <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.625em;vertical-align:-0.1944em"></span><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0359em">y</span></span></span></span> for a given task <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.4306em"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">x</span></span></span></span>. This is augmented by two auxiliary rewards, each addressing a distinct challenge in learning parallel orchestration. The reward <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>parallel</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{parallel}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.7167em;vertical-align:-0.2861em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em">r</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0278em;margin-right:0.05em"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">parallel</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.2861em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> is introduced to mitigate <em class="italic text-(--Labels-Secondary)">serial collapse</em>—a local optimum where the orchestrator defaults to single-agent execution. By incentivizing subagent instantiation, this term encourages the exploration of concurrent scheduling spaces. The <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>finish</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{finish}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.5806em;vertical-align:-0.15em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em">r</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0278em;margin-right:0.05em"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">finish</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> reward focuses on the successful completion of assigned subtasks. It is used to prevent <em class="italic text-(--Labels-Secondary)">spurious parallelism</em>, a reward-hacking behavior in which the orchestrator increases parallel metrics dramatically by spawning many subagents without meaningful task decomposition. By rewarding completed subtasks, <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>finish</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{finish}}</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.5806em;vertical-align:-0.15em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal" style="margin-right:0.0278em">r</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3361em"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:-0.0278em;margin-right:0.05em"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight"><span class="mord text mtight"><span class="mord mtight">finish</span></span></span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> enforces feasibility and guides the policy toward valid and effective decompositions. The hyperparameters <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_1</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8444em;vertical-align:-0.15em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3011em"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">1</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> and <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_2</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.8444em;vertical-align:-0.15em"></span><span class="mord"><span class="mord mathnormal">λ</span><span class="msupsub"><span class="vlist-t vlist-t2"><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.3011em"><span style="top:-2.55em;margin-left:0em;margin-right:0.05em"><span class="pstrut" style="height:2.7em"></span><span class="sizing reset-size6 size3 mtight"><span class="mord mtight">2</span></span></span></span><span class="vlist-s">​</span></span><span class="vlist-r"><span class="vlist" style="height:0.15em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> are annealed to zero over the course of training.</p>
<p>To further force parallel strategies to emerge, we introduce a computational bottleneck that makes sequential execution impractical. Instead of counting total steps, we evaluate performance using <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Critical Steps</strong>, a latency-oriented metric inspired by the critical path in parallel computation:</p>

class="vlist" style="height:0.4374em"><span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span></span> reflects the slowest subagent at each stage. Under this metric, spawning more subtasks only helps if it shortens the critical path.</p>
<p><img src="https://statics.kimi.ai/blogs/k2-5/orchestrator-1.png" alt="Architecture diagram of Kimi K2.5 Agent Swarm showing an Orchestrator dynamically creating and assigning tasks to specialized sub-agents for parallel execution" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<blockquote class="border-l-4 border-(--Colors-KMBlue) bg-(--Fills-F1) px-5 py-4 rounded-r-lg rounded-l-none my-6 [&amp;_p]:m-0 [&amp;_p]:text-(--Labels-Primary)">
<p>An agent swarm has an orchestrator that dynamically creates specialized subagents (e.g., AI Researcher, Physics Researcher, Fact Checker) and decomposes complex tasks into parallelizable subtasks for efficient distributed execution.</p>
</blockquote>
<p><img src="https://statics.kimi.ai/blogs/k2-5/20260126-225846.png" alt="Training metrics for Kimi K2.5 showing Training Accuracy and Average Parallelism both increasing steadily with RL flops during the reinforcement learning process" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<blockquote class="border-l-4 border-(--Colors-KMBlue) bg-(--Fills-F1) px-5 py-4 rounded-r-lg rounded-l-none my-6 [&amp;_p]:m-0 [&amp;_p]:text-(--Labels-Primary)">
<p>In our parallel-agent reinforcement learning environment, the reward increases smoothly as training progresses. At the same time, the level of parallelism during training also gradually increases.</p>
</blockquote>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="/en/agent-swarm" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">K2.5 Agent Swarm</a></strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">improves performance on complex tasks through parallel, specialized execution.</strong> In our internal evaluations, it leads to an <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">80%</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">reduction in end-to-end runtime</strong> while enabling more complex, long-horizon workloads, as shown below.</p>
<p><img src="https://statics.kimi.ai/blogs/k2-5/20260127-131347.jpeg" alt="Benchmark comparison: Kimi K2.5 Agent Swarm outperforming Claude Opus 4.5 on BrowseComp, Wide Search, and In-house Bench" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<p><img src="https://statics.kimi.ai/blogs/k2-5/complpexity_of_tasks.png" alt="Execution Time to Solve Tasks of Different Complexity" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<blockquote class="border-l-4 border-(--Colors-KMBlue) bg-(--Fills-F1) px-5 py-4 rounded-r-lg rounded-l-none my-6 [&amp;_p]:m-0 [&amp;_p]:text-(--Labels-Primary)">
<p>Agent Swarm reduces the minimum critical steps required to achieve target performance by 3×–4.5× compared to single-agent execution in wide search scenario, with savings scaling as targets rise—translating to up to 4.5× wall-clock time reduction via parallelization.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>Here are representative <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">trajectories</strong> demonstrating <a href="/en/agent-swarm" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">K2.5 Agent Swarm</a> in action:</p>
<!--$?--><template id="B:2"></template><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<h2 node="[object Object]">3. Office Productivity</h2>
<p>Kimi K2.5 brings agentic intelligence into <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">real-world knowledge work.</strong></p>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)"><a href="/en/agent" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">K2.5 Agent</a></strong> can <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">handle high-density, large-scale office work end to end.</strong> It reasons over large, high-density inputs, coordinates multi-step tool use, and delivers expert-level outputs: documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, and slide decks—directly through conversation.</p>
<p>With a focus on real-world professional tasks, we design <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">two internal expert productivity benchmarks</strong>. The <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">AI Office Benchmark</strong> evaluates end-to-end Office output quality, while the <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">General</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Agent Benchmark</strong> measures multi-step, production-grade workflows against human expert performance. Across both benchmarks, <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">K2.5 shows</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">59.3% and 24.3% improvements over K2 Thinking</strong>, reflecting stronger end-to-end performance on real-world tasks.</p>
<p><img src="https://statics.kimi.ai/blog/k2-5/20260127-152311.png" alt="Benchmark results: Kimi K2.5 showing significant improvements over K2 Thinking, with 71.2% better performance in AI Office Bench and 39.0% in General-Agent Bench" loading="lazy" decoding="async" node="[object Object]"/></p>
<div style="text-align:center"><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Internal Expert Productivity Bench (AI Office)</strong></div>
<br/>
<p>K2.5 agent supports advanced tasks such as <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">adding annotations in Word, constructing financial models with Pivot Tables, and writing LaTeX equations in PDFs</strong>, while scaling to long-form outputs like <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">10,000-word papers or 100-page documents</strong>.</p>
<p>Tasks that once took hours or days now complete in minutes. Here are some examples:</p>
<!--$?--><template id="B:3"></template><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<h2 node="[object Object]">4. Conclusion</h2>
<p>Grounded in advances in coding with vision, agent swarms, and office productivity, Kimi K2.5 represents a meaningful step toward AGI for the open-source community, demonstrating strong capability on real-world tasks under real-world constraints. Looking ahead, we will push further into the frontier of agentic intelligence, redefining the boundaries of AI in knowledge work.</p>
<h2 node="[object Object]">Appendix</h2>
<h3 node="[object Object]">Benchmark table</h3>
<div data-blog-hero-width="true"><div class="my-4 animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)" style="min-height:360px"></div></div>
<p>To reproduce official <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Kimi-K2.5</strong> benchmark results, we recommend using the <a href="https://platform.kimi.com/" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">official API</a>. For third-party providers, refer to <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Kimi Vendor Verifier (KVV)</strong> to choose high-accuracy services. Details: <a href="/en/blog/kimi-vendor-verifier" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">https://www.kimi.com/blog/kimi-vendor-verifier</a></p>
<h2 node="[object Object]">Footnotes</h2>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">1. General Testing Details</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>We report results for Kimi K2.5 and DeepSeek-V3.2 with thinking mode enabled, Claude Opus 4.5 with extended thinking mode, GPT-5.2 with xhigh reasoning effort, and Gemini 3 Pro with a high thinking level. For vision benchmarks, we additionally report results for Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking.</li>
<li>Unless otherwise specified, all Kimi K2.5 experiments were conducted with temperature = 1.0, top-p = 0.95, and a context length of 256k tokens.</li>
<li>Benchmarks without publicly available scores were re-evaluated under the same conditions used for Kimi K2.5 and are marked with an asterisk (*).</li>
<li>We could not evaluate GPT-5.2 xhigh on all benchmarks due to service stability issues. For benchmarks that were not tested, we mark them as &quot;-&quot;.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">2.</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Text and Reasoning</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>HLE, AIME 2025, HMMT 2025 (Feb), GPQA-Diamond and IMO-AnswerBench were evaluated with a maximum completion budget of 96k tokens.</li>
<li>Results for AIME and HMMT are averaged over 32 runs (avg@32); GPQA-Diamond over 8 runs (avg@8).</li>
<li>For HLE, we report scores on the full set (text &amp; image). Kimi K2.5 scores 31.5 (text) and 21.3 (image) without tools, and 51.8 (text) and 39.8 (image) with tools. The DeepSeek-V3.2 score corresponds to its text-only subset (marked with †) . Hugging Face access was blocked to prevent potential data leakage. HLE with tools uses simple context management: once the context exceeds a threshold, only the latest round of tool messages is retained.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">3.</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Tool-Augmented / Agentic Search</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Kimi K2.5 was equipped with search, code-interpreter, and web-browsing tools for HLE with tools and all agentic search benchmarks.</li>
<li>Except for BrowseComp (where K2.5 and DeepSeek-V3.2 used the discard-all strategy), no context management was applied, and tasks exceeding the supported context length were directly counted as failed.</li>
<li>The test system prompts emphasize deep and proactive tool use, instructing models to reason carefully, leverage tools, and verify uncertain information. Full prompts will be provided in the technical report.</li>
<li>Results for Seal-0 and WideSearch are averaged over four runs (avg@4).</li>
</ul>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">4.</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Vision Benchmarks</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Max-tokens = 64k, averaged over three runs (avg@3).</li>
<li>ZeroBench (w/ tools) uses max-tokens-per-step = 24k and max-steps = 30 for multi-step reasoning.</li>
<li>MMMU-Pro follows the official protocol, preserving input order and prepending images.</li>
<li>GPT-5.2-xhigh had ~10% failure rate (no output despite 3 retries), treated as incorrect; reported scores likely underestimate true performance.</li>
<li>WorldVQA, a benchmark designed to evaluate atomic vision-centric world knowledge. Access WorldVQA at <a href="https://github.com/MoonshotAI/WorldVQA" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">https://github.com/MoonshotAI/WorldVQA</a>.</li>
<li>OmniDocBench Score is computed as (1 − normalized Levenshtein distance) × 100, where a higher score denotes superior accuracy.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">5.</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Coding Tasks</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>Terminal-Bench 2.0 scores were obtained with the default agent framework (Terminus-2) and the provided JSON parser. In our implementation, we evaluated Terminal-Bench 2.0 under non-thinking mode. This choice was made because our current context management strategy for the thinking mode is incompatible with Terminus-2.</li>
<li>For the SWE-Bench series of evaluations (including verified, multilingual, and pro), we used an internally developed evaluation framework. This framework includes a minimal set of tools—bash tool, createfile tool, insert tool, view tool, strreplace tool, and submit tool—along with tailored system prompts designed for the tasks. The highest scores were achieved under non-thinking mode.</li>
<li>The score of Claude Opus 4.5 on CyberGym is reported under the non-thinking setting.</li>
<li>All reported scores of coding tasks are averaged over 5 independent runs.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">6.</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Long-Context Benchmarks</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>AA-LCR: scores averaged over three runs (avg@3).</li>
<li>LongBench-V2: identical prompts and input contexts standardized to ~128k tokens.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">7.</strong> <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Agent Swarm</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>BrowseComp (Swarm Mode): main agent max 15 steps; sub-agents max 100 steps.</li>
<li>WideSearch (Swarm Mode): main and sub-agents max 100 steps.</li>
</ul></div></section></div></div><!--$--><!--/$--></main><footer id="site-footer" class="bg-[#121212]" data-show-log-id="_R_fb9fivb_"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-360 px-6 tablet:px-12
